rows.stem: Electrolysis of water is a decomposition reaction. The mass ratio \((\mathrm{M_H} : \mathrm{M_O})\) of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated at the electrodes during electrolysis of water is :
rows.solution:
Electrolysis decomposes water as \(\mathrm{2H_2O \rightarrow 2H_2 + O_2}\). Two moles of hydrogen gas (\(2 \times 2 = 4\) g) are released for every mole of oxygen gas (32 g).

So the mass ratio of hydrogen to oxygen is \(4 : 32 = 1 : 8\), which is option (D) 1 : 8.

rows.stem: The products formed when Aluminium and Magnesium are burnt in the presence of air respectively are :
rows.solution:
Aluminium is trivalent and magnesium is divalent, while oxygen is divalent. So their oxides are \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) (aluminium oxide) and \(\mathrm{MgO}\) (magnesium oxide):

\(\mathrm{4Al + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2Al_2O_3}\) and \(\mathrm{2Mg + O_2 \rightarrow 2MgO}\).

This is option (B) \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) and \(\mathrm{MgO}\).

rows.stem:
The following table shows the pH values of four solutions A, B, C and D on a pH scale :

The solutions A, B, C and D respectively are of a

options.label: A
options.text: Strong acid, weak acid, neutral, strong base

options.label: B
options.text: Weak acid, neutral, weak base, strong base

options.label: C
options.text: Weak acid, neutral, strong base, weak base

options.label: D
options.text: Weak acid, neutral, strong base, strong acid

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the positions of A, B, C and D (pH 5, 7, 13 and 3) are marked only on the printed pH scale. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
Read the pH of each solution off the scale: the first at pH 5, the second at pH 7, the third at pH 13 and the fourth at pH 3.

pH 5 is a weak acid, pH 7 is neutral, pH 13 is a strong base and pH 3 is a strong acid.

So in order they are weak acid, neutral, strong base, strong acid, which is option (D) Weak acid, neutral, strong base, strong acid.

rows.stem:
Consider the following reactions :

(i) Dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide.

(ii) Magnesium oxide reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid.

(iii) Carbon dioxide reacts with sodium hydroxide.

It is found that in each case :
rows.solution:
(i) An acid and a base react to give a salt and water: \(\mathrm{HCl + NaOH \rightarrow NaCl + H_2O}\).

(ii) A metal oxide is basic, so with an acid it gives a salt and water: \(\mathrm{MgO + 2HCl \rightarrow MgCl_2 + H_2O}\).

(iii) A non-metal oxide is acidic, so with a base it gives a salt and water: \(\mathrm{CO_2 + 2NaOH \rightarrow Na_2CO_3 + H_2O}\).

In every case a salt and water are formed, which is option (A) Salt and water is formed.

rows.stem: Reaction between two elements A and B, forms a compound C. A loses electrons and B gains electrons. Which one of the following properties will *not* be shown by compound C ?

options.label: B
options.text: It is highly soluble in water.

options.label: C
options.text: It has weak electrostatic forces of attraction between its oppositely charged ions.

options.label: D
options.text: It conducts electricity in its molten state or aqueous solution.

rows.solution:
One element loses electrons and the other gains them, so the compound formed is ionic. Ionic compounds have high melting points, dissolve in water and conduct electricity when molten or in solution, because they are held together by STRONG electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions.

The property such a compound will not show is weak forces of attraction between its ions, which is option (C) It has weak electrostatic forces of attraction between its oppositely charged ions.

rows.stem: The metals obtained from their molten chlorides by the process of electrolytic reduction are :
rows.solution:
Metals high in the reactivity series, such as sodium, calcium, magnesium and aluminium, cannot be reduced by carbon, so they are obtained by electrolytic reduction of their molten chlorides (or, for aluminium, of the molten oxide). Gold, silver and iron are less reactive and are obtained by other methods.

So the metals in question are calcium and magnesium, which is option (B) Calcium and magnesium.

rows.stem: The formation of magnesium oxide is correctly shown in option :

options.label: A
options.text: Diagram (A) as printed - an electron-dot scheme for the formation of magnesium oxide; see the attached figure.

options.label: B
options.text: Diagram (B) as printed - an electron-dot scheme for the formation of magnesium oxide; see the attached figure.

options.label: C
options.text: Diagram (C) as printed - an electron-dot scheme for the formation of magnesium oxide; see the attached figure.

options.label: D
options.text: Diagram (D) as printed - an electron-dot scheme for the formation of magnesium oxide; see the attached figure.

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - all four options are drawn electron-dot schemes for the formation of magnesium oxide; the options ARE the figure. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
Magnesium (2, 8, 2) loses its two valence electrons and oxygen (2, 6) gains them. This gives one \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\) ion and one oxide ion \(\mathrm{O^{2-}}\) with a complete octet, forming MgO.

The correct diagram shows both electrons moving from one magnesium atom to one oxygen atom, giving \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{[O]^{2-}}\). The other diagrams transfer only one electron, use two oxygen atoms, or use two magnesium atoms, and so do not give MgO. This is option (A).

rows.stem: Secretion of less saliva in mouth will effect the conversion of :

options.label: B
options.text: fats into fatty acids and glycerol

rows.solution:
Saliva contains salivary amylase, which breaks down starch into simple sugars in the mouth. Less saliva means less of this conversion. (Proteins are digested in the stomach and small intestine, and fats in the small intestine.)

The process affected is starch into simple sugars, which is option (C) starch into simple sugars.

rows.stem: The plant hormone whose concentration stimulates the cells to grow longer on the side of the shoot which is away from light is :
rows.solution:
When light falls on one side of a shoot, auxin diffuses towards the shaded side. Its higher concentration there makes the cells on the side away from the light grow longer, so the shoot bends towards the light.

The hormone is auxin, which is option (D) Auxins.

rows.stem:
The correct/true statement(s) for a bisexual flower is/are :

(i) They possess both stamen and pistil.

(ii) They possess either stamen or pistil.

(iii) They exhibit either self-pollination or cross-pollination.

(iv) They cannot produce fruits on their own.
rows.solution:
A bisexual flower has both stamens and pistil, so statement (i) is true and (ii) is false.

Because it has both, it can be self-pollinated or cross-pollinated, so (iii) is true. It can also produce fruit on its own, so (iv) is false.

The true statements are (i) and (iii), which is option (C) (i) and (iii).

rows.stem: If pea plants with round and green seeds (RRyy) are crossed with pea plants having wrinkled and yellow seeds (rrYY), the seeds developed by the plants of \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation will be :
rows.solution:
Round (R) is dominant over wrinkled (r), and yellow (Y) is dominant over green (y).

RRyy gives only Ry gametes and rrYY gives only rY gametes, so every \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plant is RrYy. Each carries a dominant allele for both traits, so all the seeds are round and yellow.

This is option (C) 100% round and yellow.

rows.stem:
The breakdown of glucose has taken the following pathway :

Glucose \(\xrightarrow{\text{(a)}}\) Pyruvate + Energy \(\xrightarrow{\text{(b)}}\) Lactic acid + Energy

The sites ‘a’ and ‘b’ respectively are :

options.label: A
options.text: Mitochondria and Oxygen deficient muscle cells

options.label: B
options.text: Cytoplasm and Oxygen rich muscle cells

options.label: D
options.text: Cytoplasm and Oxygen deficient muscle cells

rows.solution:
Step (a), glucose to pyruvate (glycolysis), happens in the cytoplasm of every cell.

Step (b), pyruvate to lactic acid with release of energy, is anaerobic respiration. It happens in muscle cells when they are short of oxygen, for example during vigorous exercise.

So the sites are the cytoplasm and oxygen-deficient muscle cells, which is option (D) Cytoplasm and Oxygen deficient muscle cells.

rows.stem:
Mirror ‘X’ is used to concentrate sunlight in solar furnace and Mirror ‘Y’ is fitted on the side of the vehicle to see the traffic behind the driver. Which of the following statements are true for the two mirrors ?

(i) The image formed by mirror ‘X’ is real, diminished and at its focus.

(ii) The image formed by mirror ‘Y’ is virtual, diminished and erect.

(iii) The image formed by mirror ‘X’ is virtual, diminished and erect.

(iv) The image formed by mirror ‘Y’ is real, diminished and at its focus.
rows.solution:
Mirror X concentrates sunlight in a solar furnace, so it is a concave mirror. Sunlight comes from infinity, so the image is real, highly diminished and at the focus: statement (i) is true and (iii) is false.

Mirror Y is a rear-view mirror, so it is a convex mirror. It always forms a virtual, diminished and erect image: statement (ii) is true and (iv) is false.

The true statements are (i) and (ii), which is option (A) (i) and (ii).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: An old person is suffering from an eye defect caused by weakening of ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of the eye lens. If the defect of vision is ‘a’ which can be corrected by lens ‘b’, then ‘a’ and ‘b’ respectively are :
rows.solution:
Weakening of the ciliary muscles and loss of flexibility of the eye lens with age is presbyopia. A person with presbyopia often has both near and far vision defects, which is corrected with bifocal lenses.

So the defect and its correction are presbyopia and bifocal lens, which is option (B) presbyopia and bifocal lens.

rows.stem:
Which of the following groups do *not* constitute a food chain ?

(i) Wolf, rabbit, grass, lion

(ii) Plankton, man, grasshopper, fish

(iii) Hawk, grass, snake, grasshopper, frog

(iv) Grass, snake, wolf, tiger
rows.solution:
A food chain must start with a producer and pass to consumers in order.

(i) Grass, rabbit, wolf, lion can be arranged as a food chain. (iii) Grass, grasshopper, frog, snake, hawk is a food chain.

(ii) has plankton, grasshopper, fish and man, but a grasshopper does not feed on plankton, and (iv) has grass with snake, wolf and tiger, none of which eats grass. Neither forms a food chain.

So the groups that do not constitute a food chain are (ii) and (iv), which is option (D) (ii) and (iv).

rows.stem: The percentage of solar energy which is *not* converted into food energy by the leaves of green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem is about :
rows.solution:
Green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem capture only about 1% of the solar energy falling on their leaves and convert it into food energy. So about 99% is not converted.

This is option (D) 99%.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Decomposition reactions are generally endothermic reactions.

**Reason (R) :** Decomposition of organic matter into compost is an exothermic process.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Most decomposition reactions need energy, in the form of heat, light or electricity, to break the reactant down, so they are generally endothermic. The Assertion is true.

Decomposition of organic matter into compost releases heat, so it is exothermic. The Reason is also true, but it is an exception and does not explain why decomposition reactions in general are endothermic.

So both statements are true, but the Reason does not explain the Assertion, which is option (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** A human child bears all the basic features of human beings.

**Reason (R) :** It looks exactly like its parents, showing very little variations.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
A human child bears all the basic features of human beings, because DNA copying in reproduction passes on the body design. The Assertion is true.

But a child does not look exactly like its parents: sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents and produces variations. So the Reason is false.

So the Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** No two magnetic field lines are found to cross each other.

**Reason (R) :** The compass needle cannot point towards two directions at the point of intersection of two magnetic field lines.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Two magnetic field lines never cross, so the Assertion is true.

At any point the field has only one direction, the one a compass needle points along. If two field lines crossed, the needle would have to point in two directions at once, which is impossible. This is exactly why the lines cannot cross, so the Reason is true and explains the Assertion.

This is option (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The amount of ozone in the atmosphere began to drop sharply in the 1980s.

**Reason (R) :** The oxygen atoms combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The amount of ozone in the atmosphere began to drop sharply in the 1980s, largely because of synthetic chemicals such as CFCs. The Assertion is true.

Ozone does form when oxygen atoms combine with molecular oxygen, \(\mathrm{O + O_2 \rightarrow O_3}\), so the Reason is true. But this explains how ozone is formed, not why its amount fell.

So both statements are true, but the Reason does not explain the Assertion, which is option (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

rows.stem:
A student performs the following experiment in his school laboratory.

List two observations to justify that in this experiment a chemical change has taken place.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the reagents (dilute sulphuric acid on Zn granules in a corked conical flask) are named only as labels on the drawing. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
In the flask, zinc granules react with dilute sulphuric acid:

\(\mathrm{Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2}\)

Two observations show that a chemical change has taken place:

1. Bubbles of a gas (hydrogen) are evolved around the zinc granules.

2. The temperature changes: the flask becomes warm.

rows.stem: Draw labelled diagrams to show different stages of budding in *Hydra*.
rows.solution:
Budding in Hydra is drawn in stages:

1. A small outgrowth, the bud, forms on the side of the parent Hydra because of repeated cell division at that spot.

2. The bud grows larger and develops a mouth and tentacles of its own.

3. The fully formed bud detaches from the parent and lives as a new, independent Hydra.

The diagrams should label the parent body, the bud and the tentacles.

rows.stem: Besides minimising the loss of blood, why is it essential to plug any leak in a blood vessel ? Name the component of blood which helps in this process and state how this component perform this function.
rows.solution:
Plugging a leak in a blood vessel does more than stop blood loss: it prevents the blood pressure from falling, so the pumping system keeps working efficiently.

The component of blood that does this is the platelets. They help the blood to clot at the site of injury, which plugs the leak.

rows.stem:
(i) The transport system in plants is relatively slower than in animals. Give reasons.

(ii) State the role of phloem in the transport of materials in plants.
rows.solution:
(i) Plants have low energy needs, because a large proportion of their cells (in tissues such as wood) are dead, and plants do not move about. So a relatively slow transport system is enough for them.

(ii) Phloem carries out translocation: it moves the soluble products of photosynthesis from the leaves to the other parts of the plant. It also carries amino acids and other substances to storage organs such as roots, fruits and seeds, and to growing parts.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem: An object is placed at a distance of 60 cm from a concave lens of focal length 30 cm. Use lens formula to find the position of the image formed in this case.
rows.solution:
For a concave lens the focal length is negative: \(f = -30\) cm. The object is in front of the lens: \(u = -60\) cm.

Lens formula: \(\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{30} - \dfrac{1}{60} = -\dfrac{3}{60}\).

So \(v = -20\) cm. The image is formed 20 cm from the lens, on the same side as the object (it is virtual and erect).

rows.stem: A wire of resistance R is cut into three equal parts. If these three parts are then joined in parallel, calculate the total resistance of the combination so formed.
rows.solution:
Cutting the wire into three equal parts gives three pieces of resistance \(\dfrac{R}{3}\) each, since resistance is proportional to length.

In parallel: \(\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{R/3} + \dfrac{1}{R/3} + \dfrac{1}{R/3} = \dfrac{3}{R} + \dfrac{3}{R} + \dfrac{3}{R} = \dfrac{9}{R}\).

So the total resistance is \(R_p = \dfrac{R}{9}\).

rows.stem: Define electric power. When do we say that the power consumed in an electric circuit is 1 watt ?
rows.solution:
Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed or dissipated in a circuit, that is, the electrical energy consumed per unit time: \(P = VI\).

The power consumed is 1 watt when a current of 1 A flows through a circuit with a potential difference of 1 V across it, that is, when 1 J of electrical energy is consumed in 1 s.

rows.stem: “Excessive use of chemicals and pesticides in agriculture adversely effect the environment.” Justify this statement.
rows.solution:
Chemicals and pesticides used on crops are washed into the soil and into water bodies, where they affect both the living and the non-living parts of the ecosystem.

Most of them are non-biodegradable. They enter the food chain and accumulate progressively at each trophic level, a process called biological magnification. So the organisms at every trophic level are harmed, and those at the highest level, including human beings, carry the greatest concentration.

rows.stem:
(a) “Displacement reactions also play a key role in extracting metals in the middle of the reactivity series.” Justify this statement with two examples.

(b) Why can metals high up in the reactivity series not be obtained by reduction of their oxides by carbon ?
rows.solution:
(a) A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from its compound. Aluminium, being more reactive, reduces the oxides of metals in the middle of the series to the metal, releasing a lot of heat:

\(\mathrm{3MnO_2(s) + 4Al(s) \rightarrow 3Mn(l) + 2Al_2O_3(s)} +\) heat

\(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3(s) + 2Al(s) \rightarrow 2Fe(l) + Al_2O_3(s)} +\) heat

The second, the thermite reaction, gives molten iron and is used to join broken railway tracks.

(b) Metals high in the reactivity series, such as sodium, magnesium and calcium, have a greater affinity for oxygen than carbon has. So carbon cannot remove the oxygen from their oxides, and these metals are obtained by electrolytic reduction instead.

rows.stem: With the help of an activity, explain the conditions under which iron articles get rusted.
rows.solution:
Take three test tubes and put clean iron nails in each.

1. In the first, pour some ordinary water and cork it. The nails are exposed to both air and water.

2. In the second, pour boiled distilled water and add about 1 mL of oil, then cork it. Boiling removes dissolved air, and the oil layer stops air dissolving again, so the nails are exposed to water only.

3. In the third, put some anhydrous calcium chloride and cork it. It absorbs any moisture, so the nails are exposed to dry air only.

After a few days the nails rust in the first test tube only. So iron rusts only when it is exposed to both air (oxygen) and water (moisture).

rows.stem:
(i) Name two metals which react violently with cold water. List any three observations which a student notes when these metal are dropped in a beaker containing water.

(ii) Write a test to identify the gas evolved (if any) during the reaction of these metals with water.
rows.solution:
(i) Sodium and potassium (lithium also) react violently with cold water. When they are dropped into water, the student observes:

1. A violent reaction takes place.

2. A large amount of heat is given out.

3. The hydrogen gas evolved may catch fire.

(ii) The gas is hydrogen. Bring a burning splinter near the gas collected: it burns with a pop sound.

rows.stem:
Plants have neither a nervous system nor muscles, even then they respond to stimuli. For example, the leaves of *chhui-mui* (touch-me-not) plant when touched begin to fold up and droop.

(a) How is the information communicated in “touch-me-not” plants ?

(b) What enables the plant cells to bring out the observable response ?

(c) Differentiate the movement mentioned above from the movement of tendrils in a pea plant.
rows.solution:
(a) Plant cells communicate the information that a touch has occurred by electrical-chemical means, passing it from cell to cell (there is no nervous tissue).

(b) The plant cells change shape by changing the amount of water in them, swelling or shrinking. This produces the observable folding and drooping.

(c) The folding of touch-me-not leaves is independent of growth and does not depend on the direction of the stimulus (a nastic movement). The movement of tendrils in a pea plant is a growth movement towards the support, that is, it depends on the direction of the stimulus (a tropic movement).

rows.stem:
(a) What are chromosomes ?

(b) Explain in brief how stability of DNA content of a species is ensured in sexually reproducing organisms ?
rows.solution:
(a) Chromosomes are thread-like structures in the nucleus. They carry the genes, in the form of DNA, which hold the information for inheriting features from parents to the next generation.

(b) Each body cell has two copies of each chromosome, one from each parent. When germ cells (gametes) form, the number of chromosomes is halved, so each gamete carries only one set.

When a male and a female gamete fuse, the zygote gets one set from each, which restores the normal number of chromosomes. So the amount of DNA stays the same from generation to generation.

rows.stem: Draw ray diagrams to show the nature, position and relative size of the image formed by a convex mirror when the object is placed (i) at infinity and (ii) between infinity and pole P of the mirror.
rows.solution:
(i) Object at infinity: draw rays parallel to the principal axis striking the convex mirror. After reflection they appear to diverge from the focus F behind the mirror (the reflected rays are produced backwards as dotted lines to meet at F). The image is at F, behind the mirror; it is virtual, erect and highly diminished (point-sized).

(ii) Object between infinity and the pole P: draw one ray from the top of the object parallel to the axis, which reflects as if coming from F, and a second ray aimed at the centre of curvature C, which reflects back along itself. The two reflected rays, produced backwards, meet behind the mirror between P and F. The image is there; it is virtual, erect and diminished.

Arrows must be drawn on the rays: the marking scheme deducts half a mark if they are missing.

rows.stem:
Consider the following electric circuit :

Calculate the values of the following :

(a) The total resistance of the circuit

(b) The total current drawn from the source

(c) Potential difference across the parallel combination of \(10\,\Omega\) and \(15\,\Omega\) resistors
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit (10 Ω and 15 Ω in parallel, in series with 60 Ω and 40 Ω in parallel, a 15 V battery, key K and ammeter A) is given only as a drawing. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
(a) The 10 \(\Omega\) and 15 \(\Omega\) resistors are in parallel: \(\dfrac{1}{R_1} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{5}{30}\), so \(R_1 = 6\,\Omega\).

The 60 \(\Omega\) and 40 \(\Omega\) resistors are in parallel: \(\dfrac{1}{R_2} = \dfrac{1}{60} + \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{5}{120}\), so \(R_2 = 24\,\Omega\).

The two combinations are in series, so the total resistance is \(6 + 24 = 30\,\Omega\).

(b) \(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{15}{30} = 0{\cdot}5\) A.

(c) The whole current passes through the first combination, so the potential difference across it is \(V = IR_1 = 0{\cdot}5 \times 6 = 3\) V.

rows.stem:
(a) Write the relationship between resistivity and resistance of a cylindrical conductor of length *l* and area of cross-section A. Hence derive the SI unit of resistivity.

(b) Why are alloys used in electrical heating devices ?
rows.solution:
(a) The resistance of a uniform cylindrical conductor is proportional to its length and inversely proportional to its area of cross-section: \(R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A}\), where \(\rho\) is the resistivity of the material.

So \(\rho = \dfrac{RA}{l}\), and its SI unit is \(\dfrac{\text{ohm} \times \text{metre}^2}{\text{metre}} = \text{ohm metre}\) (\(\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\)).

(b) An alloy has a higher resistivity than its constituent metals, so it produces more heat, and it does not oxidise (burn) readily at high temperatures. So alloys are used in electrical heating devices such as irons and toasters.

rows.stem:
(i) Draw two isomeric structures of Butene \((\mathrm{C_4H_8})\).

(ii) Name the following compounds :

(I) \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}Cl}\)

(II) \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CO{-}CH_3}\)

(iii) Write the chemical equations for the following reactions. Mention one essential condition each for these reactions to take place.

(I) Ethanol undergoes complete oxidation

(II) Propene undergoes hydrogenation

(III) Ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the two compounds in (ii) are printed as full structural formulas; the stem carries their condensed formulas, which name the same compounds. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
(i) Butene \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\) has isomers that differ in the position of the double bond or in the chain, for example:

But-1-ene: \(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH{-}CH_2{-}CH_3}\)

But-2-ene: \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH{=}CH{-}CH_3}\)

(2-methylpropene, \(\mathrm{CH_2{=}C(CH_3){-}CH_3}\), is a third.) In the answer each is drawn as a full structural formula showing every hydrogen.

(ii) (I) \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}Cl}\) is chloropropane (1-chloropropane).

(II) \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CO{-}CH_3}\) is butanone (butan-2-one).

(iii) (I) Ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid by alkaline potassium permanganate (or acidified potassium dichromate) on heating:

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{alkaline } KMnO_4 \text{ + heat}} CH_3COOH}\)

(II) Propene adds hydrogen in the presence of a nickel or palladium catalyst:

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CH_2 + H_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni / Pd}} CH_3CH_2CH_3}\)

(III) Ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol in the presence of an acid catalyst to form an ester:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
(i) A carbon compound X is a good solvent. On reaction with sodium, X forms two products Y and Z. Z is used to convert vegetable oil into vegetable ghee. Identify and name X, Y and Z. Also write the equation of reaction of X with sodium to justify your answer.

(ii) Write chemical equation to show what happens when ethanol :

(I) burns in oxygen/air.

(II) is heated at 443 K in excess conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\).

(III) reacts with acidified potassium dichromate.
rows.solution:
[CBSE marking scheme: the printed combustion equation \(\mathrm{2C_2H_5OH + 7O_2 \rightarrow 4CO_2 + 6H_2O}\) is not balanced (16 oxygen atoms on the left, 14 on the right); it needs \(\mathrm{6O_2}\). The scheme awards the mark for an unbalanced equation in any case.]

(i) X is ethanol (\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}\)), a good solvent. With sodium it forms Y, sodium ethoxide (\(\mathrm{C_2H_5ONa}\)), and Z, hydrogen gas (\(\mathrm{H_2}\)). Hydrogen is used to convert vegetable oil into vegetable ghee by hydrogenation.

\(\mathrm{2CH_3CH_2OH + 2Na \rightarrow 2CH_3CH_2ONa + H_2}\)

(ii) (I) Ethanol burns in oxygen to give carbon dioxide and water, with heat and light:

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2CO_2 + 3H_2O}\) + heat + light

(II) Heated at 443 K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid, ethanol is dehydrated to ethene:

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{conc. } H_2SO_4, \ 443\,K} C_2H_4 + H_2O}\)

(III) Acidified potassium dichromate oxidises ethanol to ethanoic acid:

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{acidified } K_2Cr_2O_7} CH_3COOH}\)

rows.stem:
(i) Write the functions of the following parts of human female reproductive system :

(I) Ovary

(II) Fallopian tube

(III) Uterus

(ii) State briefly two contraceptive methods used by human males.
rows.solution:
(i) (I) Ovary: produces the female gametes (eggs) and the female hormones such as oestrogen.

(II) Fallopian tube (oviduct): carries the egg from the ovary to the uterus, and is the site of fertilisation.

(III) Uterus: the site of implantation of the embryo and of its development.

(ii) Two contraceptive methods used by males:

1. Mechanical barrier: a condom, which stops sperm from reaching the egg.

2. Surgical method: vasectomy, in which the vas deferens is blocked or cut so that sperm cannot pass out.

rows.stem:
(i) Differentiate between self-pollination and cross-pollination.

(ii) Identify A, B and C in the diagram given below and write one function of each.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (ii) asks to identify the parts labelled A, B and C on a drawn pistil (stigma, pollen tube, female germ-cell); the labels exist only in the drawing. Page idx 20.
rows.solution:
(i) In self-pollination, pollen grains are transferred from the stamen to the stigma of the same flower. In cross-pollination, pollen grains are transferred from the stamen of one flower to the stigma of another flower of the same species.

(ii) The diagram shows a pistil with a germinating pollen grain.

A is the stigma: it receives the pollen and provides a suitable environment for it to germinate.

B is the pollen tube: it carries the male germ cells (gametes) down to the female gamete in the ovary.

C is the egg cell (female germ cell): it fuses with a male gamete to form the zygote.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem:
(i) The power of a lens ‘X’ is \(-2{\cdot}5\) D. Name the lens and determine its focal length in cm. For which eye defect of vision will an optician prescribe this type of lens as a corrective lens ?

(ii) “The value of magnification ‘m’ for a lens is \(-2\).” Using new Cartesian Sign Convention and considering that an object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the optical centre of this lens, state :

(I) the nature of the image formed;

(II) size of the image compared to the size of the object;

(III) position of the image, and

(IV) sign of the height of the image.

(iii) The numerical values of the focal lengths of two lenses A and B are 10 cm and 20 cm respectively. Which one of the two will show higher degree of convergence/divergence ? Give reason to justify your answer.

(i) Draw a ray diagram to show the refraction of a ray of light through a rectangular glass slab when it falls obliquely from air into glass.

(ii) State Snell’s law of refraction of light.

(iii) Differentiate between the virtual images formed by a convex lens and a concave lens on the basis of :

(I) object distance, and

(II) magnification.
rows.solution:
(i) Draw a rectangular glass slab with a ray of light falling obliquely on its upper surface. At the air-glass surface the ray bends towards the normal. It travels straight through the glass, and at the glass-air surface it bends away from the normal. The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but laterally displaced. Mark the angles of incidence and refraction at each face, and draw arrows on the rays: the marking scheme deducts half a mark if they are missing.

(ii) Snell's law: for light of a given colour and a given pair of media, the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is a constant, \(\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \text{constant}\).

(iii) (I) A convex lens forms a virtual image only when the object is placed between its optical centre O and its focus F. A concave lens forms a virtual image wherever the object is placed in front of it.

(II) The virtual image formed by a convex lens is magnified; that formed by a concave lens is diminished.

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: Write balanced chemical equations to show the products formed during electrolysis of brine.
rows.context: Seawater contains many salts dissolved in it. Common salt is separated from these salts. Deposits of solid salt are also found in several parts of the world. These large crystals are often brown due to impurities. This is called rock salt and is mined like coal. The common salt is an important raw material for chemicals of daily use.
rows.solution:
Electrolysis of brine (a concentrated solution of sodium chloride) gives sodium hydroxide, hydrogen and chlorine:

\(\mathrm{2NaCl(aq) + 2H_2O(l) \xrightarrow{\text{electricity}} 2NaOH(aq) + H_2(g) + Cl_2(g)}\)

This is the chlor-alkali process. Chlorine is given off at the anode and hydrogen at the cathode.

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: List two uses of any one product obtained during electrolysis of brine.
rows.context: Seawater contains many salts dissolved in it. Common salt is separated from these salts. Deposits of solid salt are also found in several parts of the world. These large crystals are often brown due to impurities. This is called rock salt and is mined like coal. The common salt is an important raw material for chemicals of daily use.
rows.solution:
Any two uses of any one product, for example:

Sodium hydroxide: degreasing metals, making soaps and detergents, paper making, artificial fibres.

Chlorine: water treatment and swimming pools, making PVC, disinfectants, bleaching powder.

Hydrogen: as a fuel, making margarine, making ammonia for fertilisers.

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: A mild non-corrosive basic salt ‘A’, used for faster cooking, is strongly heated to produce a compound ‘B’, that is used for removing permanent hardness of water. Identify A and B and also write the equation for the reaction that occurs when A is heated.
rows.context: Seawater contains many salts dissolved in it. Common salt is separated from these salts. Deposits of solid salt are also found in several parts of the world. These large crystals are often brown due to impurities. This is called rock salt and is mined like coal. The common salt is an important raw material for chemicals of daily use.
rows.solution:
The mild, non-corrosive basic salt used for faster cooking is baking soda, sodium hydrogencarbonate \(\mathrm{NaHCO_3}\).

On strong heating it gives sodium carbonate \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}\), which (after recrystallisation as washing soda) is used to remove permanent hardness of water.

\(\mathrm{2NaHCO_3 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Na_2CO_3 + H_2O + CO_2}\)

So the salt is sodium hydrogencarbonate and the compound formed is sodium carbonate.

rows.stem: Define water of crystallisation. Give two examples of salts that have water of crystallisation.
rows.context: Seawater contains many salts dissolved in it. Common salt is separated from these salts. Deposits of solid salt are also found in several parts of the world. These large crystals are often brown due to impurities. This is called rock salt and is mined like coal. The common salt is an important raw material for chemicals of daily use.
rows.solution:
Water of crystallisation is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt.

Examples (any two): copper sulphate pentahydrate \(\mathrm{CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O}\) (blue vitriol); washing soda \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\); gypsum \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O}\); ferrous sulphate heptahydrate \(\mathrm{FeSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O}\) (green vitriol).

rows.stem: Name and define the process by which green plants prepare food.
rows.context: The maintenance functions of all living organisms must go on even when they are not doing anything particular. Even when we are just sitting in a class or even asleep, this maintenance job has to go on. These maintenance processes require energy to prevent damage and break-down of cells and tissues, which is obtained by the individual organism from the food prepared by the autotrophs, called producers.
rows.solution: The process is photosynthesis: the process by which green plants use the energy of sunlight, absorbed by chlorophyll, to convert carbon dioxide and water into carbohydrates, releasing oxygen.

rows.stem: Write chemical equation involved in the above process.
rows.context: The maintenance functions of all living organisms must go on even when they are not doing anything particular. Even when we are just sitting in a class or even asleep, this maintenance job has to go on. These maintenance processes require energy to prevent damage and break-down of cells and tissues, which is obtained by the individual organism from the food prepared by the autotrophs, called producers.
rows.solution: \(\mathrm{6CO_2 + 12H_2O \xrightarrow[\text{Sunlight}]{\text{Chlorophyll}} C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 + 6H_2O}\)

rows.stem: State in proper sequence the events that occur in synthesis of food by desert plants.
rows.context: The maintenance functions of all living organisms must go on even when they are not doing anything particular. Even when we are just sitting in a class or even asleep, this maintenance job has to go on. These maintenance processes require energy to prevent damage and break-down of cells and tissues, which is obtained by the individual organism from the food prepared by the autotrophs, called producers.
rows.solution:
The events of photosynthesis, in sequence:

1. Absorption of light energy by chlorophyll.

2. Conversion of light energy into chemical energy, and splitting of water into hydrogen and oxygen.

3. Reduction of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates.

Desert plants keep their stomata closed during the day to save water. They take up carbon dioxide at night and store it as an intermediate, which is then acted upon by the energy absorbed by chlorophyll during the day.

rows.stem:
Explain giving reasons what happens to the rate at which the green plants will prepare food

(I) during cloudy weather, and

(II) when stomata get blocked due to dust.
rows.context: The maintenance functions of all living organisms must go on even when they are not doing anything particular. Even when we are just sitting in a class or even asleep, this maintenance job has to go on. These maintenance processes require energy to prevent damage and break-down of cells and tissues, which is obtained by the individual organism from the food prepared by the autotrophs, called producers.
rows.solution:
(I) During cloudy weather the rate of photosynthesis decreases, because less sunlight is available to supply the energy for the process.

(II) When the stomata are blocked by dust the rate decreases, because the exchange of gases, especially the intake of carbon dioxide, is reduced.

rows.stem: Write the colours of the insulation covers of the line wires through which supply comes to our homes.
rows.context: In our homes, we receive the supply of electric power through a main supply also called mains, either supported through overhead electric poles or by underground cables. In our country the potential difference between the two wires (live wire and neutral wire) of this supply is 220 V.
rows.solution: The live wire has red insulation and the neutral wire has black insulation.

rows.stem: What should be the current rating of the electric circuit (220 V) so that an electric iron of 1 kW power rating can be operated ?
rows.context: In our homes, we receive the supply of electric power through a main supply also called mains, either supported through overhead electric poles or by underground cables. In our country the potential difference between the two wires (live wire and neutral wire) of this supply is 220 V.
rows.solution:
Power \(P = 1\) kW \(= 1000\) W and \(V = 220\) V.

\(P = VI\), so \(I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{1000}{220} \approx 4{\cdot}54\) A.

The circuit must carry more than this, so its current rating should be 5 A.

rows.stem: What is the function of the earth wire ? State the advantage of the earth wire in domestic electric appliances such as electric iron.
rows.context: In our homes, we receive the supply of electric power through a main supply also called mains, either supported through overhead electric poles or by underground cables. In our country the potential difference between the two wires (live wire and neutral wire) of this supply is 220 V.
rows.solution:
The earth wire provides a low-resistance conducting path for current. If any current leaks to the metallic body of an appliance, the earth wire carries it to the earth and keeps the body at the potential of the earth.

So the user of an appliance such as an electric iron does not get a severe electric shock.

rows.stem: List two precautions to be taken to avoid electrical accidents. State how these precautions prevent possible damage to the circuit/appliance.
rows.context: In our homes, we receive the supply of electric power through a main supply also called mains, either supported through overhead electric poles or by underground cables. In our country the potential difference between the two wires (live wire and neutral wire) of this supply is 220 V.
rows.solution:
Two precautions:

1. Use a fuse of the correct rating in the circuit. If the current becomes too large (because of overloading or a short circuit), the fuse wire melts and breaks the circuit, preventing damage to the circuit and the appliances.

2. Connect appliances with a metallic body to the earth wire. Any leakage current then flows to the earth, which prevents an electric shock.
